method: Completed differential source review against reviewed Windows GNU AVX512. Corrected parser strips semicolon comments and splits inline labels before excluding data/directives. Normalizes numeric spelling, whitespace, prefetch byte-ptr and explicit RIP syntax. Branches resolved to instruction positions and checked through SequenceMatcher equal-block insertion mapping; all residual blocks inspected. Directives and labeled constants inspected in v143. Equivalent instructions not independently serial-reread.
findings: Corrected comparison counts2539 GNU and2542 MSVC executable instruction records,2532 identical normalized instructions and23 matching branch targets. Earlier2541/2548 counts are superseded invalid previews, not additional instructions.

Only two residual blocks remain. Initial counter carry uses explicit unsigned vpcmpud predicate1 instead of vpcmpltud alias; ADD1 broadcasts into YMM6 before masked additions. YMM6 is overwritten by key broadcast before use as compression state, so source scratch lifetime is consistent.

Sixteen-counter update explicitly broadcasts ADD16/ADD1 into ZMM4/5 then masked register additions and unsigned comparison. These compression registers have already been stored as output; next outer iteration reinitializes them. No live CV preservation defect inferred from temporary reuse.

All23 control-flow targets land at corresponding unchanged instructions after accounting for three additional instructions. Hash-many and scalar Windows register/frame adaptations match GNU apart from these reviewed blocks.

PUBLIC/PROC aliases,16-byte code alignment and64-byte read-only constant alignment reviewed separately. Constant INDEX0/1,ADD0/1/16,block length and IV declarations match source values. XOF-many remains absent in this Windows variant.
limits: 288/289 pinned blobs reviewed;150/500 complete repositories. Remaining rmlint file xxhash.h.
Text/control-flow equivalence is not MASM build, relocation, unwind, x86 runtime, guard-page or performance proof. pHash/ASAN remains deferred.
